questions.q: What does the Law of Leadership say?
a: Being first in a market makes leadership likely
The cheapest product usually wins the market
The best product always becomes the leader
Advertising matters more than timing
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the first mover advantage, which gives a product time ahead of rivals.

questions.q: What should you do if a rival reached the market before you?
a: Become the first brand in customers’ minds
Copy the leader’s product exactly
Undercut the leader on price
Wait for the leader to make a mistake
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains the Law of the Mind, where the name people think of first tends to lead.

questions.q: How did Walmart avoid competing head-on with existing retailers?
a: It created the discount retail category
It opened stores only in small towns
It sold goods at a loss for years
It copied its rivals’ store formats
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Sam Walton did not invent retailing but invented the discount retail chain.

questions.q: What does the Law of Sacrifice say about offering many products?
a: The more you offer, the less focus each one gets
The more you offer, the more customers return
Each extra product lowers your costs
Wide ranges protect you from rivals
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that specialists win, because focus is traded away with every extra product.

questions.q: What does the Pepsi example teach about choosing an audience?
a: Trying to appeal to everyone rarely works
Young buyers are always the most profitable
Older customers resist trying new brands
Rival brands should be imitated closely
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes Pepsi did well with young people but could not win over committed Coke drinkers.
